definition: how sharply I can read one of my own resources

settled:
The ladder has six rungs. Not knowing a resource exists, knowing it exists, telling enough from not enough, a stoplight read against my own distribution, numbered levels on an absolute scale, and a real number.

The thing underneath is continuous. A rung is where a change becomes something I can consciously tell apart, and I do not commit to whether that line is in my body or in my perception. What I track is how cleanly I can read it.

Ten years of minute-level energy accounting on myself is what carries my bars up to real numbers.

At the top of the ladder I can say exactly which resource is draining, how fast it goes, and what drains it.

A bar climbs by being the bottleneck, and a real number costs years of being it. Health is the only bar that has paid those years. Safety sits at numbered levels after about a year as the bottleneck, which is where I would expect it. Mana and stamina are still at the stoplight.

A bar I only read as a gate may never need a real number at all.
